statement: Intel launched an underwritten public offering of $15 billion of common stock (up to $17.25 billion with the underwriters' option), with proceeds earmarked for general corporate purposes including capital expenditures, citing 'unprecedented investment in AI compute' as the demand backdrop.
why: A raise of this size funds capacity — advanced packaging, external wafers and purpose-built silicon — which over time adds a non-NVIDIA source of AI compute supply and of packaging capacity that is currently the binding constraint.

impact.mechanism: Equity proceeds directed at capital expenditure expand Intel's foundry and advanced-packaging capacity, increasing alternative supply of AI silicon and of the packaging step that gates merchant-GPU output.

evidence.excerpt: Intel is launching an underwritten public offering of $15 billion of common stock
Customers continue to signal a strong and sustainable demand environment, driven by unprecedented investment in AI compute.
physical AI, purpose-built silicon, advanced packaging and external wafers

confidence.basis: Company newsroom release read at secondary tier; the offering was not yet priced and the corresponding SEC free-writing prospectus returned HTTP 403, so final terms could not be confirmed from a filing.

dispersion: Base deal $15B; up to $17.25B if underwriters exercise the 30-day option for an additional $2.25B. Capex context (2026 above $20B, 2027 'significantly above') comes from secondary reporting, not the release text.
